paper.title: LLM-Planner: Few-Shot Grounded Planning for Embodied Agents with Large Language Models
paper.central_claim: LLM-Planner uses less than 0.5% of paired instruction/plan training data, yet achieves competitive embodied instruction-following success against fully supervised baselines; physically grounded dynamic replanning improves few-shot plans in partially observed environments.

evidence.quote: We adopt a k-nearest-neighbor (kNN) retriever to select the in-context examples (Section 4.3 ). We also use logit biases [ 10 ] to further constrain the output space of the LLM to the allowed set of actions and objects. With all the above designs, we have obtained the static version of LLM-Planner, which can already generate reasonable HLPs. In Section 4.4 , we propose a novel grounded re-planning algorithm to enhance LLMs with the ability to ground to the current environment, which further improves the HLP quality. Finally, we discuss how to integrate LLM-Planner into existing embodied agents to empower them with few-shot planning capabilities in Section
evidence.support_explanation: Retrieval-conditioned static planner, logit constraints and grounded dynamic replanning are separate steps.

evidence.quote: we use the ground truth object information to construct an oracle value function. As we described in §5.3, this gives SayCan an unfair competitive advantage by giving it the oracle knowledge of all objects and affordances in the current environment a priori to compiling the list of skills. Even though SayCan can shrink the skill space with the extra knowledge, SayCan’s ranking nature calls LLM significantly more times than a generative model like LLM-Planner. In fact, LLM-Planner calls GPT-3 avg.

signatures.operation: Retrieve 9 similar demonstrations, complete action/object high-level plan with logit bias to legal output tokens.
signatures.output: Semantic (action,object) subgoal sequence for fixed HLSM low-level executor.
signatures.conditions: Similarity must capture relevant task structure; pretrained executor/object detector must implement legal subgoals.
signatures.feedback: Static generation initially; dynamic variant consumes observed objects and completed prefix.
signatures.selection_rule: Prompt design selected by LOOCV on the same 100 training pairs, not independent additional validation labels.
signatures.data: 100 paired annotations, NOT 100 total perception/navigation training trajectories; nonlanguage modules are separately pretrained.
signatures.persistence: Static 100-example reference bank and fixed pretrained modules; no online parameter update or growing verified library.
signatures.later_use: Retrieve demonstrations again for each new episode.
signatures.failure_boundary: Full-data HLSM can outperform; microwave detection can dominate despite correct planning.

signatures.object: Open-loop HLP execution under partial observability
signatures.information: Current object-detector list (>80% confidence per implementation), current environment and completed subgoals; no proposed-method test metadata oracle.
signatures.operation: Replan on low-level failure/stagnation or fixed action horizon, retain completed prefix and update remaining subgoals with observed objects.
signatures.output: Updated legal HLP rather than restarting completed tasks.
signatures.conditions: Detector fidelity and correspondence of HLSM completion/failure events to actual state.
signatures.feedback: Execution progress/failure and observed object inventory.
signatures.selection_rule: Event/horizon-triggered replacement within the same episode.
signatures.data: ALFRED official seen/unseen splits; same HLSM low-level modules for static/dynamic comparison.
signatures.persistence: Episode-local prefix only; no retained harness optimization.
signatures.later_use: Continue current task with revised suffix.
signatures.failure_boundary: Object misses and low-level failures remain; algorithmic notation alone does not establish verifier calibration.

gap.author_gap: Embodied instruction following consumes expensive paired language trajectories and static LLM plans are not grounded in the changing environment.
gap.checked_gap: Few-shot paired-language data is a genuine bottleneck conditional on substantial existing low-level training. Dynamic replanning adds a modest online gain over an already strong static retrieval prompt.

lineage.method: HLSM hierarchical planner/controller, FILM, SayCan language-affordance ranking, LLM in-context example retrieval
lineage.source_version: 2212.04088v3 related work and Appendix A descriptions; external original versions not independently fixed/read

gap.closest_adjacent: HLSM supplies the same executor; retrieval prompting supplies plan generation; SayCan already grounds skill selection. Residual is efficient generative few-shot HLP plus object-aware suffix replanning.
gap.residue: Low paired-data planners fail even though perception/navigation policies are available; open-loop plans cannot react to unexpected object observations.
gap.stakes: Annotations and model retraining impede new tasks; perception errors can still erase planner gains.
gap.method_response: Retrieve contextual plans, constrain action/object output and condition replanning on current objects/completed prefix.
gap.remaining_gap: Not total-data-free; same low-level detector creates severe task failures. Budget-matched ablation of all interactions and broader embodied domains absent.
unresolved: No comprehensive foundation-model pretraining overlap audit.
Original adjacent versions not externally verified under fixed-material restriction.

expectations.source_strength: common_practice; literature-derived, not an actual reviewer quotation
source_refs: - **E01 (ablation, common_practice).** Hold the frontier backbone fixed and compare the proposed harness with at least one alternative harness or loop organization on the same episodes. For zero-shot VLN-CE the alternative is a rerun of a published zero-shot harness or workflow (2606.10577#s4, 2609.15195#s4) with the same model; for coding agents, a second deployable harness. — _applies when_ a claim that a harness (rather than the model) raises embodied or agentic success.
expectations.applies_when: a claim that a harness (rather than the model) raises embodied or agentic success.
expectations.reason: Static/dynamic variants share text-davinci-003 and HLSM; primary local gain uses fixed executor.

expectations.source_strength: common_practice; literature-derived, not an actual reviewer quotation
source_refs: - **E02 (ablation, common_practice).** Attribute a gain to a harness component only through one-at-a-time toggles (leave-one-out or single add) with the backbone fixed. A cumulative stack (A, then +B, then +C) or a bundle-level comparison does not separate components or their interactions. — _applies when_ a claim that a specific harness component (depth tool, memory, verifier, skill library, plugin, feedback channel) causes the improvement.

expectations.source_strength: common_practice; literature-derived, not an actual reviewer quotation
source_refs: - **E04 (reproducibility, common_practice).** Report run-to-run variance and use paired task-level statistics: repeated runs per setting, bootstrap or permutation CIs over tasks, and sign tests on discordant episodes. A single run on a 100-episode subset is treated as descriptive. In the read single-run papers, differences of a few points sit within noise. — _applies when_ any success-rate comparison between harnesses, models or training recipes on a fixed task subset.
expectations.applies_when: any success-rate comparison between harnesses, models or training recipes on a fixed task subset.
expectations.reason: Official split success and task-type breakdown provided; no repeated rollout variance or paired confidence test for small dynamic gain.

Harnesses with similar pass rates can differ about 40x in tokens per solved task. — _applies when_ a claim that a harness, interface or distilled student is better or more practical than an alternative.

claims.baseline/control: Few-shot HLSM/FILM and fully supervised references; distinguish goal-only from step instructions
claims.data_budget: 100 paired annotations vs21k full; no equality of total pretrained data
claims.selection_vs_test: 100-pair LOOCV prompt selection; official test/validation seen/unseen evaluations
claims.result: Few-shot dynamic goal-only test-unseen SR13.41; fully trained HLSM20.27. Step-instruction dynamic16.42 vs few-shot HLSM0.61/FILM0.20; scaling valid-unseen full-data17.80 vs HLSM18.28.

claims.allowed_conclusion: Strong efficiency for paired language labels conditional on available pretrained embodiment modules, not total-data or total-cost efficiency.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Author-reported ALFRED end-to-end success shows paired-label-efficient frozen-LLM planning and a modest fixed-HLSM replanning gain on unseen test scenes, conditional on pretrained perception/navigation modules.

G.reason: Concrete paired-annotation and partial-observability bottlenecks; HLSM/SayCan lineage clear locally, with remaining low-level dependence acknowledged.

M.reason: Retrieval, legal-output bias and object-aware suffix revision align with gap; nearest-neighbor coverage and perception remain assumptions.

X.reason: Reference bank, semantic executor interface and event handback reconstructable, but no calibrated success-monitor audit or cross-domain recipe.

measurement.reason: Environment-scored official task SR and goal-condition metrics exist, but no repeated execution per evaluation episode; anchors-v2 single-shot ceiling applies despite large benchmark coverage.

causality.reason: Fixed-HLSM static/dynamic and retrieval/logit toggles support local effects; budget mismatch and oracle-adapted SayCan weaken comprehensive attribution.

holdout.reason: Training-pair LOOCV and official unseen test scenes support separation; structural task-category and foundation pretraining overlap not audited, one embodied benchmark.

statistics.reason: Substantial official split and task-type breakdown including microwave failure, but no repeated-rollout variance or CIs; count/absence-of-variance band1–2, not top band.

cost.reason: Average calls7 vs22 is useful inference-cost evidence; tokens, low-level training, wall time and equal-budget dynamic control missing.
